jobs.title: Workshop Director - CIO Advisory / AI
jobs.description:
Position Purpose

Infotech's members come to us for our advisory services, value added research, and our passion for driving measurable business results. If you are looking to be part of an IT research firm that relentlessly creates innovative advisory products and transformational IT research solutions, we would like to speak with you. You will work for a rapidly growing company that understands the importance of supporting employees through flexibility, inclusiveness, learning and development, internal career mobility, measurement of the Employee Experience and actioning on employee feedback and building strong relationships.

Due to continued growth in our workshop offering, we are expanding our team of talented professionals to support our member base. We offer a high learning, dynamic, and progressive culture focused on evolving the field of information technology. This role is ideal for someone who -

Excels in Leveraging practical experience to improve client strategies, processes, and project execution.
Has subject matter expertise in one of more of the following subject areas.
Strategy and governance; leadership; project portfolio management; enterprise architecture; service management; service desk; IT operations; infrastructure management; data management; enterprise applications; application development; security and risk management.

Excels in facilitating and engaging cross-functional groups of IT and business professionals via interactive presentations, training and/or workshops.
Excels in Learning and flexibly communicating IT best practices to meet the needs of diverse organizations, industries, situations, and audiences.

What You Will Do, Includes, But Not Limited To

As a Workshop Director you will be actively engaged in delivering measurable value to Infotech's members by utilizing our IT Best Practice methodologies, detailed in our Blueprints, to deliver online or on-site structured 1-week workshops designed to help improve their strategies, processes, and organizational effectiveness.

Duties & Responsibilities

Engagement Scoping: Work with clients over the phone to properly scope and formalize the objectives, agenda, deliverables, and overall workshop effort in advance of online or onsite delivery.
Workshop Delivery: Lead the delivery of four-day workshops, online or onsite, based on Infotech’s Best Practice Methodology Blueprints.
Work with client cross-functional teams to define the scope and outcomes of their IT initiatives / projects, perform capability maturity assessments, and gap analyses, and identify member improvement opportunities/recommendations.
Client Service: Identify client need for continued advisory service and support after the workshop.
Assist in the development of Statements of Work to formalize the objective, agenda, and deliverables of workshops.

Commercial Activity: Identify opportunities to provide additional advisory services, workshop, consulting engagements, and services to our clients after the workshop.
Research Support: Transmit new knowledge and lessons learned during workshop interactions to influence and improve the research agenda and content. On occasion, develop client case studies and/or industry research notes.
Contribute to Infotech research by developing client case studies and/or industry research notes.
Generate insight and providing expertise to assist with the development of our research content.

Collaboration & Support: Work collaboratively with others to:
Design and build high-quality keynote/other presentations, and successful delivery of presentations as needed.
Play a lead role in building internal AI capabilities at Infotech, including internal agent development, tool prototypes, knowledge sharing and AI-enhanced workflows.

Education & Experience

To be successful, you will need:

Undergraduate degree in Business, IT, or related discipline. MBA is an asset or equivalent.
Minimum of 5-10+ years progressive experience in IT leadership OR consulting roles within medium to large organizations (IT team size between 25 and 500 FTEs).
Consulting roles within large organizations is a definite advantage
Acquired experience in more than one of the following areas:
IT Strategy, IT Governance (COBIT, ITIL), Organizational Structure, Digital Business, IT Cost, IT Risk Management, Business Relationship Management, Service Catalog, Service Management,
AI Strategy, AI Governance, AI Literacy, Agentic AI, various AI tools knowledge,

Especially valuable experience (definite advantage) in more than one of the following:
Enterprise Architecture, Security, Zero Trust, Ransomware, Risk, Privacy, Information Security,
IT Service Desk/Operations, Infrastructure/Cloud Strategy, Disaster Recovery Planning, Asset Management, Cloud Operations, Incident & Problem Management,
Data Strategy, Data Governance, Enterprise Content Management,
Application Development, Enterprise Application (ERP/HRIS/CRM/ECM) selection and Implementation, Rationalization, SDLC,
Agile, Project Portfolio Management, Resource Management, Digital Product,

Superior interpersonal, communication, and presentation skills, exceptional ability to work well with others.
The ability, flexibility, and enthusiasm to work in a fast-paced, rapidly growing, and energetic environment.
Previous experience presenting to a C-Suite audience.
Certifications in an IT or project management related topic e.g. PMP, COBIT 5, ITIL are considered beneficial
Deep understanding of current and emerging technologies, how other enterprises are employing them to drive digital business, and how they may be applied to the enterprise to drive digital business.

Skills

Client Interaction and Facilitation; Ability to build rapport and communicate effectively with clients and particularly through the facilitation of workshops online or in-person with an audience of 5 to 20 clients (mid management to executive management).
Exceptional presentation, facilitation, writing, interpersonal communication, and collaboration skills.
Public Speaking ability to speak to a larger group (50+) of individuals

Problem solving; decision making, knowledge management, managing through change & uncertainty and dynamic learning mindset
Client Advisory and Service Delivery; lead multiple clients through complex projects by providing guidance, critical analysis, and support
Proven ability to build rapport, credibility, and trust with clients at all levels and across all disciplines. Build client relationships and established themselves as a trusted advisor (SME) in their space
Opportunity Identification and Definition; lead multiple clients through structured working sessions; can facilitate an inclusive discussion in order to meet clear objectives
Project Management; ability to work independently and remotely for extended periods of time.

Travel Requirement:
This role will involve travel, for on-site engagements. Willingness and ability to travel 50% of the time (2 weeks per month) is required. Must hold a valid driver’s licence.

Visa Requirement:
Must be eligible to obtain appropriate work Visa for cross-border work within North America and globally.

Work Hours Requirements:
Must be available for after-hours work periodically to service Global (Americas/EMEA/APAC) clients.

Language Skills
: Bilingual proficiency in French, Spanish or German is preferred to support our diverse client base across North America and globally.

To that end, upon request, Infotech will ensure, to the extent possible, that accommodation be made available to applicants throughout the recruitment and hiring process.

jobs.description:
SysAid is a leading IT Service Management (ITSM) platform helping organizations deliver exceptional service experiences. As we evolve our platform with innovations like Spaces
and SAI
, we are redefining how IT teams operate—and how customers realize value.
We are entering a critical phase where AI is not just a feature—but a growth driver
, both for our customers and our internal operating model.
We are seeking a Director of Customer Retention & Growth
to own SysAid’s net revenue retention (NRR)
and lead the transformation of our post-sales organization into an AI-enabled, insight-driven growth engine
.
This leader will harness agentic AI
to:
Help customers achieve faster, measurable outcomes
Drive proactive, data-driven engagement
Scale internal operations without linear headcount growth

Key Responsibilities

1. Own Net Revenue Retention (NRR)

Drive strategy across:
Churn reduction
Expansion (upsell, cross-sell)
Build AI-enhanced forecasting models for:
Churn risk
Expansion propensity
Establish clear ownership across CSMs, AMs, and lifecycle stages

2. Drive AI-Powered Adoption & Time-to-Value

Ensure customers adopt:
Core ITSM capabilities
Spaces (new interface)
SysAid’s agentic AI capabilities

Partner with Product & PS to:
Embed AI into onboarding journeys (e.g., AI-generated onboarding plans)
Deliver guided, automated adoption experiences

Operationalize AI-driven health scoring and next-best actions

3. Build a Scalable, AI-Driven Growth Engine

Design a structured expansion motion powered by AI:
Identify expansion signals automatically (usage, gaps, triggers)
Use AI to generate:
Deal insights
Business cases
Pricing recommendations
Equip teams with AI copilots
for:
Account planning
QBR preparation
Executive storytelling
Shift from reactive selling to predictive, insight-led growth

4. Reduce Churn Through Proactive, Automated Risk Management

Build AI agents
to:
Continuously monitor customer health
Detect risk patterns (product usage, support friction, sentiment)
Trigger automated or human-led interventions
Move from: Reactive service tickets → to Predictive, system-driven retention plays

Identify systemic churn drivers (e.g., Spaces gaps, onboarding issues) and close the loop with Product

5. Lead Agentic AI Transformation (Internal + Customer-Facing)

Customer-Facing AI

Define how customers should use SysAid’s agentic AI to:
Automate IT workflows
Improve service delivery
Increase ROI from the platform
Partner with Product to:
Package AI use cases into clear value propositions
Define “when to use an agent” vs traditional workflows/integrations

Ensure CSMs can articulate and drive adoption of AI outcomes—not just features

Internal AI & Automation

Deploy AI agents to transform post-sales operations:
Automated QBR generation
Call summaries and action tracking
Ticket clustering and root cause analysis
Renewal and expansion insights
Increase coverage per CSM
through automation and AI augmentation
Redesign workflows to minimize manual work and maximize customer-facing time

6. Elevate Customer Experience Through Intelligent Feedback Loops

Use AI to:
Aggregate and cluster customer feedback (support tickets, calls, surveys)
Identify product and experience trends at scale
Reduce noise from service records and surface true systemic issues

Create structured, data-backed feedback loops into Product (especially for Spaces)

7. Redefine Roles for an AI-First Organization

Evolve team responsibilities:
CSMs → Outcome Orchestrators

AMs → Growth Strategists

Support → AI Supervisors

Train teams to:
Leverage AI in daily workflows
Interpret AI-generated insights
Focus on high-value, human interactions

8. Build & Lead a High-Performing, AI-Native Team

Define segmentation and coverage models enhanced by AI
Establish KPIs across:
Retention & expansion
Adoption (including AI feature adoption)
Operational efficiency (automation rates, productivity)
Hire and develop talent comfortable operating in an AI-augmented environment

Key Success Metrics

Net Revenue Retention (NRR)
Gross Churn Rate
Expansion Revenue
Adoption of:
Core platform (including Spaces)
Agentic AI capabilities
Time-to-Value
Customer Health Score Accuracy
% of workflows automated (internal & customer-facing)
CSM productivity (accounts per CSM, time spent on strategic vs. manual work)

You've done this before:

3-5+ years in channel sales, partner management, or a multi-stakeholder commercial role
Experience with technology resellers, VARs, or MSPs in a B2B SaaS context
Carried a revenue number tied to a partner network and hit it
Salesforce as a sales system, not just a database. You know what a clean pipeline looks like and why it matters
ITSM or IT management familiarity is a strong advantage, not a requirement

You operate this way

Every deal has a next step, a close date, and an honest stage: not a wish list.
You get energy from recruiting a new partner and getting them to the first deal, not just managing an existing book.
You communicate proactively: partners know where their deals stand without having to ask.
You treat partner feedback as data: document it, escalate it, follow up.
You're comfortable with ambiguity and find it motivating to create structure where none exists.

This is probably not the right fit if...

You need a fully built PRM, mature playbooks, and established workflows before you can be productive
You treat CRM as something you fill out for your manager rather than how you run your business
You've never been accountable for a revenue number tied to a partner network

jobs.description:
Description & Requirements

Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. A place where creativity thrives, new perspectives are invited, and ideas matter. A team where everyone makes play happen.

Electronic Arts creates next-level entertainment experiences that inspire players and fans around the world. Here, everyone is part of the story. Part of a community that connects across the globe. A place where creativity thrives, new perspectives are invited, and ideas matter. A team where everyone makes play happen.

The Game Developer Experience (GDX) organization, part of EA's Central Technology group, powers the foundational platforms, tools, and infrastructure that enables engineers, artists, designers, and creators across over 20 global studios to build world-class games. Game development operates at an extraordinary technical scale—requiring massive binary and 3D asset pipelines, multi-terabyte monolithic repositories, high-throughput global edge caching and sync architectures, distributed build and test farms, and seamless multi-engine workflows.

Our mission is to simplify game creation at scale, eliminate workflow friction, and empower developers to spend their time innovating for players rather than waiting on tools and infrastructure

As a Senior Director of Product Management in the Game Developer Experience (GDX) team, you will lead a team of product managers and partner with engineering leaders across a product portfolio focused on accelerating how Electronic Arts builds games. You will report into the VP of Game Developer Experience and will solve production bottlenecks and deliver capabilities that improve developer velocity, platform reliability, and AI-enabled workflows for over 20 global game studios.

This is a technical product leadership role, and successful candidates should be able to demonstrate a strong grasp of software development workflows. Ideal candidates will have a software engineering background demonstrated through a college/university degree and/or relevant work experience.

Responsibilities

Collaborate with the Head of Engineering and studio technical leaders to define and deliver a long-term product vision and integrated roadmap across GDX.
Lead product prioritization decisions that balance immediate studio pain points (reliability, latency, stability) with long-term technical bets (cloud-native development environments and AI workflow automation).
Align leadership across Central Technology and Game Studios, advising VP- and C-level executives on portfolio trade-offs, technical dependencies, and multi-year R&D plans.
Direct the cross-company product strategy for AI-assisted game development, including coding assistants, AI-augmented content creation workflows, and evaluations of latest technologies.
Work with Studio Leaders, Legal, Security, and external technology providers to scale AI tools across thousands of creators while establishing governance, IP safeguards, and cost-effective model infrastructure.
Evaluate cloud and on-premises infrastructure costs with Engineering and Finance teams to optimize Total Cost of Ownership (TCO).
Lead a team of senior, lead, and director-level product managers, with occasional travel required.

Required Qualifications

12+ years of experience in product management, technology strategy, or platform engineering, including managing product leaders across multi-product portfolios.
5+ years of experience leading globally distributed product management teams across a portfolio including career management and establishing best practices.
Knowledge of software development lifecycles, distributed systems, hybrid infrastructure, and high-throughput build and deployment pipelines.
Experience establishing metrics, evaluate platform unit economics and TCO, manage multi-million-dollar investment trade-offs, and guide cost optimization at scale.
Experience aligning VP+ and C-level across matrixed engineering and studio organizations.
Bonus: Experience defining product strategy for developer platforms, CI/CD and source control systems, cloud infrastructure, or engineering productivity tools.
Bonus: Hands-on experience scaling Generative AI or ML-assisted developer productivity tools across large engineering or creative organizations.

Pay Transparency - North America

Compensation And Benefits

The ranges listed below are what EA in good faith expects to pay applicants for this role in these locations at the time of this posting. If you reside in a different location, a recruiter will advise on the applicable range and benefits. Pay offered will be determined based on a number of relevant business and candidate factors (e.g. education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, or business needs).

PAY RANGES

British Columbia (depending on location e.g. Vancouver vs. Victoria) *$204,600 - $287,500 CAD

Pay is just one part of the overall compensation at EA.

In Canada, we offer a package of benefits including vacation (3 weeks per year to start), 10 days per year of paid sick time, company top-up to EI/QPIP benefits up to 100% of base salary when you welcome a new child (12 weeks for maternity, and 4 weeks for parental/adoption leave), extended health/dental/vision coverage, life insurance, disability insurance, and retirement benefits to regular full-time employees. Certain roles may also be eligible for bonus and long-term cash programs.

About Electronic Arts

We’re proud to have an extensive portfolio of games and experiences, locations around the world, and opportunities across EA. We value adaptability, resilience, creativity, and curiosity. From leadership that brings out your potential, to creating space for learning and experimenting, we empower you to do great work and pursue opportunities for growth.

We adopt a holistic approach to our benefits programs, emphasizing physical, emotional, financial, career, and community wellness to support a balanced life. Our packages are tailored to meet local needs and may include healthcare coverage, mental well-being support, retirement savings, paid time off, family leaves, complimentary games, and more. We nurture environments where our teams can always bring their best to what they do.

Electronic Arts is an equal opportunity employer. All employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, national origin, ancestry, sex, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, age, genetic information, religion, disability, medical condition, pregnancy, marital status, family status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. jobs.description:
Client Summary

O2E Brands is the parent company behind three exceptional brands: 1-800-GOT-JUNK?, WOW 1 DAY PAINTING, and Shack Shine. Their core philosophy is “It’s All About People.” They operate with transparency, trust, and a growth mindset. 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? is widely recognized as the world’s largest junk-removal franchise, helping both homes and businesses reclaim space with efficient, full‑service junk removal. Backed by a visionary CEO, the company has since grown into a powerhouse in its category, operating in major metros across North America and Australia.

1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? isn’t just a junk-hauling company — it’s a scalable, high-growth franchise brand. Their financial performance, operational footprint, and consistent expansion reflect deep market penetration and strong business fundamentals.

Behind the trucks is a growing product and technology organization. O2E runs an agile product operating model in which product managers, engineers and designers work together in trios. The company is now building much of its own software from scratch, including the systems franchise partners use to run their businesses every day: dispatch, routing, capacity, and the apps crews use in the field.

Now entering the next major chapter, they’re on a mission to double the business from approximately $700M to $1.4B by transforming from a single-service brand into a multi-product, customer-obsessed growth platform. With one of North America’s most recognized and beloved brands, an energized franchise network, and a clear path to multi-business expansion, the company is poised for its most ambitious decade yet.

Highlights

Founded in 1989, HQ in Vancouver, BC
Part of the O2E Brands umbrella, founded by CEO Brian Scudamore
Brian has been featured on Oprah for his leadership, Undercover Boss, Forbes, The Wall Street Journal, The Globe and Mail, and most recently as a Dragon on Dragon's Den!
Recognized locally as a “Most Admired Corporate Culture”, a “Top 50 Small & Medium Employer”, and a “Most Engaged Workplace.”
Ranked #8 on the 2026 Top 100 Global Most Loved Workplaces®
Recognized nationally as a workplace of choice through numerous awards, including “Best Place to Work”, “Great Workplaces in Canada”, and “50 Most Engaged Workplaces.”
175 locations across Canada, the United States, and Australia
Brian Scudamore was recognized as a Top Most Loved CEO in 2024
An agile product org built on trios of PM, engineering, and design, now building new products in-house

About the Role

1-800-GOT-JUNK? is building the operational backbone for its next chapter of growth. As the business scales across a large franchise network, the systems and processes that power its operations need to be standardized, connected, and built to scale. This role leads that work, shaping the internal tools that corporate staff and front-line team members rely on every day.
Reporting to the SVP, Product, we are looking for a Director of Product (Back Office) to lead the unified product strategy and execution across Platform, Data, the Operator Portal, and the Truck Team Member (TTM) app. You will own back-office standardization and process transformation, with the goal of building scalable, reliable internal tools that maximize operational efficiency across the system.
You will lead a team of senior product managers and product managers, and ensure key stakeholders, including large franchise ownership groups with established business operations, are aligned and moving in the same direction.

Please note: this role is hybrid and based in either Kansas City (Overland Park, KS) or Vancouver, BC.

Product Strategy & Execution:

Serve as the product leadership voice for the unified back-office strategy, translating the company’s Winning Aspiration, Where We Play, and How We Win strategy into a coherent product roadmap and execution plan
Ensure the team is focused on the highest-leverage problems, without spreading effort across too many priorities
Pressure-test team approaches by challenging assumptions, validating customer insight, and grounding decisions in customer truth and the Product & Technology Strategy
Connect product strategy to operational and go-to-market realities

Process Transformation & Standardization:

Map all as-is and to-be processes across the product function using swim lane and value stream mapping, doing the work yourself
Identify overlap, gaps, and inconsistencies in how teams work, and give the SVP a clear view of what everyone does today and what they should be doing
Build a sequenced transformation roadmap that moves the org from current state to a standardized target state
Drive standardization across residential and commercial product teams in partnership with other product leaders

AI & Product Innovation:

Bring a real point of view on how AI can change product discovery, prototyping and operational workflows, well beyond conversational tools
Introduce AI tools and practices that help standardize and speed up how the product org works
Help shape how AI shows up in the products franchise partners and crews use every day

Team Leadership & Capacity Building:

Lead and develop the back-office product team, including senior product managers and product managers
Build a team environment where PMs operate with clarity, autonomy, and strong strategic context
Identify capability or capacity gaps early and flag them to the SVP, Product

Stakeholder Management & Franchise Alignment:

Ensure key stakeholders, including large franchise ownership groups, are aligned and moving in the same direction
Create a clear and respectful path for integrating franchise expertise into the formal product and revenue model
Communicate progress, decisions, and trade-offs clearly to franchise executive stakeholders, managing expectations through a period of significant change
Represent product priorities in senior leadership conversations and cross-functional planning

Organizational Agility & Decision Quality:

Keep teams moving by surfacing blockers, resolving ambiguity, and escalating where needed
Bring the right people into the right conversations at the right time
Maintain a clear view of what is decided, what is in progress, and what is still open across the product agenda

About You

You're a senior product leader who's built software for field operations and isn't afraid to roll up your sleeves. You've spent your career in tech, working closely with engineers and designers to bring new products to life, and the operational side of a business energizes you. You have the presence to hold a room of franchise owners, the empathy to actually listen to them, and the conviction not to get walked over.

10+ years in product management, including 5+ years leading and developing PMs
Hands-on experience with process transformation, including swim lane and/or value stream mapping you've done yourself, not delegated
Product experience in field operations software such as dispatch, routing, scheduling, fleet, capacity management or similar operational platforms
Background in a SaaS or tech environment, building software in an agile model and embedded with engineering and design (trio, pod or squad)
A track record of building and launching new products, not just configuring existing tools
Real AI fluency and a point of view on how it changes product work, with tools you've used and an opinion on what's good
Executive presence and adaptable communication, with experience earning buy-in from external or franchise stakeholders

Bonus:

Experience with Snowflake or a similar modern data stack
Franchise, multi-location or field services industry exposure
Lean or Six Sigma training
Experience standing up product operations practices across an org

The Extras that Matter

1-800-GOT-JUNK? is famous for its culture, and for good reason. This is a place that takes people seriously and builds things that matter to thousands of franchise partners and crews.
A direct line to the CEO's priorities, and the chance to build the operational backbone of an iconic brand

Company Profit Sharing Program
401(k): employer match up to 4% (US)
Comprehensive Extended Health & Dental Benefits
Generous paid vacation and personal days
Hybrid work environment (Overland Park, KS or Vancouver, BC)
Professional development opportunities
Health & Wellness programs

Base salary of $180K–$200K in local currency

You'll lead a team that is talented and highly motivated, and unify them behind a single vision, bringing together two distinct TPM cultures from our legacy companies, standardizing how they work, what systems they use, and how we define success. We see TPM as the connective tissue as Engineering and Product unify two platforms and redesign our PDLC/SDLC to ship faster, with higher quality, for customers.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You'll build the operating model, the career path, and the standards for the team — and you'll personally drive some of our highest-stakes technical programs to completion, with metrics that prove the impact.

Who you are:

7+ years in technical program management, with at least 2-3 years directly leading a TPM team, ideally through a merger, reorg, or other period of significant organizational change.
Track record of driving large-scale, cross-functional technical programs — platform migrations, consolidations, or major SDLC/PDLC changes — to measurable outcomes.
Experience building or substantially improving a program-management operating model: standards, career paths, SLAs, and documentation, not just running the programs within one.
Comfort partnering with distributed global teams, with genuine attention to making remote and offshore team members first-class contributors.
Strong executive communication skills — able to translate technical program risk into decisions for both engineering leaders and business stakeholders.
A bias toward bringing people together rather than picking sides — this role inherits two team cultures and needs to build a third, better one.

Fluency with industry standard dashboard/reporting tools and knowledge of how to set, visualize, measure, and create accountability through effective project- and team-level metrics.

Nice to Have

Experience operating inside a dedicated Product & Engineering Operations function, or building one.
Background in enterprise SaaS, ideally through a company merger or acquisition integration.
Experience building and managing software release cycles where quality is an imperative.

What Success Looks Like In The First Year

The TPM team operates as one function with a shared standard, regardless of legacy company origin, and all North America- and India-based TPMs report feeling fully integrated and supported.
A single, current source of truth exists for TPM engagement, role expectations, career path, and SLAs.
Technical Programs has a defined, visible seat in the PDLC/SDLC redesign, with clear metrics tracking delivery speed and quality.
Seismic’s updated PDLC and release processes are operating like clockwork with TPMs as its standard-bearers.

Reporting Line & Location

This role reports to the VP of Product & Engineering Operations. Based in Vancouver, Canada, with regular overlap hours with an India-based team; some travel for team offsite events may be required.

What you’ll be doing:

Unify the TPM team into one operating model, bringing together the two legacy TPM mindsets rather than picking one, and ensure our North America- and India-based TPMs are all fully supported, well-integrated, and highly productive.

Director, Product Management

Who is Mastercard?

Mastercard is a global technology company in the payments industry. Our mission is to connect and power an inclusive, digital economy that benefits everyone, everywhere by making transactions safe, simple, smart, and accessible. Using secure data and networks, partnerships and passion, our innovations and solutions help individuals, financial institutions, governments, and businesses realize their greatest potential.

Our decency quotient, or DQ, drives our culture and everything we do inside and outside of our company. With connections across more than 210 countries and territories, we are building a sustainable world that unlocks priceless possibilities for all.

Overview

Small and medium enterprises are the backbone of the Canadian economy. They represent more than 98% of businesses, contribute approximately 35% of Canada's GDP, and employ over half of the country's workforce. Behind these numbers are millions of entrepreneurs and business owners pursuing their ambitions, investing in growth, and shaping the future of their communities. Mastercard is committed to helping businesses move from aspiration to achievement by providing the products, partnerships, insights, and capabilities they need to grow and thrive. This segment is central to Mastercard's growth strategy, not only because of its economic impact, but also because SMEs play a vital role in the payments ecosystem as both buyers and sellers of digital payment solutions.

The Canadian Small & Medium Enterprises team is looking for a Director, Product Management to help drive our growth in the segment through solution innovation & commercialization, value proposition enhancements (core & via partnerships), distribution of Mastercard products and solutions via channel distribution channels, and P&L optimization. Execute against our strategy to capture incremental segment share and help secure market, divisional leadership

Analyze market trends, competition, and SME lifecycle journeys to inform product and go-to-market strategies, driving product differentiation and innovation 

Identify partnership opportunities to drive value proposition improvements and new distribution channels

Collaborate with the broader Commercial & New Payment Flows team to help design and execute relevant use cases to advance digital solutions for the segment

Work with other regional and divisional teams ensure sales readiness and training by developing necessary sales enablement tools for SMEs

Putting people first, every day

BDO is a firm built on a foundation of positive relationships with our people and our clients. Each day, our professionals provide exceptional service, helping clients with advice and insight they can trust. In turn, we offer an award-winning environment that fosters a people-first culture with a high priority on your personal and professional growth.

Reporting to the Chief Human Resources Officer and serving as a member of the HR Leadership Team, the Director, Talent Management & Workforce Insights
leads an integrated portfolio spanning Talent Management, Total Rewards, HR Operations and People Analytics. The Director sets priorities across the portfolio, leads experienced specialist teams and helps these capabilities evolve to better support the firm’s business and people priorities.

Working closely with HR Business Partners, Talent Acquisition and leaders across the firm, the Director will shape the talent systems, workforce insights, rewards and HR services that help BDO retain its people, create meaningful opportunities for talent, and support the firm’s evolving workforce needs. The Director leads through experienced leaders and is not expected to be the technical expert in every area of the portfolio.

Key Accountabilities

Portfolio Leadership

Lead the Organizational Development, Total Rewards, HR Operations and People Analytics portfolio, setting clear priorities, accountabilities and measures of success.
Turn the firm’s people priorities into focused plans and practical outcomes.
Use workforce data, external information and business context to identify risks and opportunities and provide clear recommendations.
Connect the work across the portfolio so leaders and employees receive clear and consistent support.
Review what is working, stop or simplify lower-value work and improve the portfolio based on evidence and business needs.
Foster strong collaboration across HR so firmwide approaches are practical, consistent and responsive to business needs.

Talent Management

Strengthen the firm’s approach to Talent Management, with an initial focus on reviewing how performance, talent and succession decisions are supported across the firm.
Work with HR Business Partners and business leaders to improve the quality and consistency of talent discussions and decisions.
Use talent data and feedback to identify firmwide themes, risks and areas requiring attention.
Clarify roles, accountabilities and ways of working across HR as these practices evolve.

Workforce Insights

Lead the firm’s workforce insights agenda by identifying the workforce questions, trends and risks that matter most to the business.
Work through the People Analytics team to strengthen the quality, relevance and use of workforce reporting and analysis.
Move the function beyond producing standard reports toward providing insights and recommendations that support business, talent and workforce decisions.
Set priorities for the People Analytics team based on the decisions and workforce questions the firm needs to address.
Work with Finance, HR Business Partners, Talent Acquisition and other stakeholders to bring together business context, workforce data and external talent-market information.
Help define how the firm’s workforce insights capability should evolve, including opportunities to make better use of analytics, technology and AI.

Total Rewards & Wellbeing

Ensure reward programs remain competitive, sustainable and aligned with business priorities, market trends and workforce needs.
Oversee the evolution of reward and recognition practices that support attraction, retention and performance.
Advance the firm’s approach to employee wellbeing, ensuring it remains responsive to evolving workforce needs and expectations and supports sustainable performance and a positive employee experience.

HR Operations & Enablement

Provide strategic oversight of HR Operations, working through the leaders responsible for day-to-day service delivery, reporting and operational performance.
Set clear priorities for improving HR processes, systems and services, with a focus on simplicity, consistency and the needs of employees, leaders and HR teams.
Sponsor practical opportunities to use technology, automation and AI to reduce manual work and improve service delivery.
Ensure the People Analytics team provides accurate, timely and useful workforce reporting and analysis.
Connect operational, reporting and technology priorities to the broader needs of HR and the business.

Stakeholder Relationships

Build trusted relationships across the firm and serve as a strategic advisor on talent, workforce and organizational matters.
Lead and develop leaders across Organizational Development, Total Rewards, HR Operations and People Analytics, setting clear priorities and building shared accountability across the portfolio.

What You Will Help Us Achieve

Success in this role means:

A more focused approach to Talent Management, including stronger performance and succession practices over time.
Competitive and sustainable reward programs that support attraction, retention, wellbeing and performance.
Workforce reporting and insights that help leaders understand workforce trends, risks and opportunities and make better decisions.
Clear roles and accountabilities across the portfolio as its capabilities evolve.
Practical use of technology, automation and AI to simplify work and improve HR delivery.

What You Bring

Significant progressive HR experience, including leadership responsibility for an enterprise talent, rewards, HR operations, workforce insights or related portfolio.
Meaningful depth in at least one of Talent Management, Total Rewards, HR Operations or People Analytics, together with the range and learning agility to lead experienced specialists across the broader portfolio.
Experience improving enterprise HR practices or functions and showing clear results.
A track record of using workforce data and insight to influence business decisions and improve outcomes.
Evidence of questioning established approaches, simplifying work and improving outcomes for the business and employees.
Practical understanding of workforce trends, technology and AI, and the judgement to apply them where they can improve decisions or ways of working.
Demonstrated ability to lead through others, set clear priorities and build shared accountability across specialist teams.
Exceptional relationship-building, communication and influencing skills, including the ability to work effectively with senior leaders.
Strong judgement and business acumen, with the ability to balance employee experience, business priorities, risk and operational realities.
Experience within professional services or another complex, relationship-driven organization would be considered a strong asset.
University degree in Human Resources, Business or a related discipline. A relevant professional designation and/or advanced degree would be considered an asset.

Why BDO?

Our people-first approach to talent has earned us a spot among Canada’s Top 100 Employers for 2026. This recognition is a milestone we’re thrilled to add to our collection of awards for both experienced and student talent experiences.

At BDO, our people experience is guided by three core pillars— Do work with genuine care, Do what matters with purpose, and Do what’s next
- shaping how we support our people, serve our clients, and grow together.

Our firm is committed to providing an environment where you can be successful in the following ways:

We enable you to engage with how we change and evolve, being a key contributor to the success and growth of BDO in Canada.
We help you become a better professional within our services, industries, and markets with extensive opportunities for learning and development.
We support your achievement of personal goals outside of the office and making an impact on your community.
We foster a collaborative, inclusive environment where your ideas are valued, and you can do your best work with genuine care and purpose
We encourage innovation and forward thinking, empowering you to embrace what’s next and help shape the future of our firm

Giving back adds up:
Where company meets community. BDO is actively involved in our communities by supporting local charity initiatives. We support staff with local and national events where you will be given the opportunity to contribute to your community.

Total rewards that matter:
We pay for performance with competitive total cash compensation that recognizes and rewards your contribution. We provide comprehensive benefits from day one, and a flexible personal time off policy. We’re committed to supporting your overall wellbeing and provide reimbursement for wellness initiatives that fit your lifestyle.

Everyone counts:
We are committed to creating a workplace where employees can participate fully, contribute meaningfully and succeed without barriers. We are dedicated to fostering a workplace defined by respect, fairness, and a true sense of belonging for everyone. We recognize and celebrate the unique experiences, identities, and perspectives that each of us bring – and that these experiences strengthen how we work together. Our commitment extends to ensuring that our application process is both inclusive and accessible. If you require accommodation to complete the application process, please contact us.

All BDO personnel are expected to spend some of their time working in the office, at the client site, and virtually unless accommodations or alternative work arrangements are in place.

Our model is a blended approach designed to support the flexible needs of our people, the firm and our clients. It’s about creating work experiences that meet everyone’s needs and providing flexibility to adjust when, where and how we work to meet the expectations of our role.

Our Code of Conduct sets clear standards for how we conduct business. It reflects our shared values and commitments and includes guiding principles to help us make ethical decisions and maintain trust with each other, our clients, and the public.

Success Factors in the Role

Sales execution becomes repeatable

Sales leaders use the tools willingly
Salesforce is used because it makes running the business easier, not because it’s mandated.

Commercial risks are visible before decisions (with a disciplined reduction process)

Fewer “surprises”

Le/La Directeur(trice), opérations commerciales corporatives est responsable de définir, standardiser et améliorer en continu le système d’exploitation commercial de l’organisation. Moins d’exceptions gérées à la pièce; un flux de dossiers plus constant à travers les mêmes étapes et approbations.

Moins d’escalades de dernière minute causées par des termes non documentés, des approbations floues ou des incohérences entre régions.

S’assurer que les leaders P&L ont la visibilité requise avant que les engagements soient pris, et non après.

Aligner la structure du funnel avec les besoins d’affaires, incluant le mix produit, la saisonnalité et la capacité.
Développer des tableaux de bord standards pour les responsables P&L et les leaders des ventes.
Réduire le bruit administratif afin que l’outil soutienne les décisions, plutôt que de devenir une couche de reporting additionnelle.
Gestion du funnel et planification des ventes
Définir et faire vivre des pratiques cohérentes à travers le groupe de gestion du funnel.
Donner une visibilité prospective sur la concentration des revenus par usine, type d’actif, industrie, représentant et autres découpages nécessaires.

Permettre une consolidation au niveau du groupe de ces données.
Contrats, termes et suivi des risques

Rendre le risque commercial mesurable, visible et discutable, plutôt qu’implicite ou anecdotique.
Formation, mobilisation et gestion des incitatifs de ventes

Développer des formations adaptées aux rôles, notamment sur Salesforce et les notions de base liées aux contrats.
Bâtir une cadence reproductible pour les rencontres de ventes afin de renforcer les thèmes clés et l’exécution.

Detailed Job Description

Position Overview

The Executive Director of Finance is responsible for providing strategic leadership and comprehensive oversight of the company’s financial management functions, including financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, cash flow management, financial analysis, and internal financial controls. This role ensures that the company’s financial operations are aligned with its overall strategic objectives, while supporting organizational growth, profitability enhancement, and long-term financial stability.

The Executive Director of Finance works closely with the Chief Financial Officer (CFO), Chief Executive Officer (CEO), senior management team, department heads, and business unit managers to develop financial strategies, evaluate business performance, manage financial resources, and provide support for key management decisions. This position plays a critical role in strengthening financial governance, improving the efficiency of financial management, and ensuring the accuracy and transparency of the company’s financial operations.

Key Responsibilities

I. Financial Strategy and Senior Leadership

Develop and implement financial strategies that align with the company’s business objectives, operational priorities, and long-term development plans. Provide financial guidance to senior management regarding investment decisions, resource allocation, cost management, and business expansion opportunities. Establish financial policies, management standards, and performance targets to strengthen financial discipline and ensure that all financial activities remain consistent with the company’s overall strategy.

II. Financial Planning, Budgeting, and Forecasting

Take full responsibility for the preparation and execution of annual budgets, periodic financial forecasts, and long-term financial plans. Coordinate with department heads and business unit leaders to set financial targets, assess capital requirements, and allocate financial resources effectively. Continuously monitor budget execution, analyze financial variances, and propose corrective or improvement measures to maintain cost efficiency and achieve established financial goals.

III. Financial Reporting and Performance Analysis

Oversee the preparation, review, and submission of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports. Ensure that financial statements, management reports, and performance analysis data are accurate, timely, and compliant with applicable accounting standards. Evaluate the company’s revenue performance, operating expenses, profitability, cash flow, and financial trends to provide actionable insights that support senior management decision-making and the improvement of business performance.

The Head of Credit & Portfolio Management is the senior leader of the Portfolio Management (PM) function across Global Corporate Banking in Canada and the U.S. The role owns PM governance, standards and risk oversight. The role partners with Risk & Financial Management, Capital Markets and Global Transaction Banking, and applies effective challenge within BMO’s Risk Appetite framework.

Governance & Standards
Act as the key governance driver for the PM function; own PM standards, policy interpretation and governance consistency across Corporate Banking.
Maintain a common PM operating playbook across LUs, standardizing intent and repeatable work rather than org models.
Provide Corporate Banking input to BMO corporate policies and lending directives, and ensure policies are interpreted and applied correctly.

Exercise delegated approval authority within delegated limits for transactions above LU PM head authority.

Foster an inclusive environment and a high-performance culture; role model One Bank leadership and the Bank’s Ambition.

Build trusted, collaborative relationships with the Front Office to embed capital discipline, optimization, and velocity considerations in portfolio decisions.
Provide actionable insights and reporting on returns, resource consumption, optimization opportunities, and capital velocity to enhance strategic decision-making at the CM level.

Leadership

Demonstrate BMO's Winning Culture behaviours including Alignment, Accountability and Recognition.
Support transformation efforts that enhance transparency, capital efficiency, balance sheet velocity, structuring effectiveness, and decision quality across Capital Markets.

Qualifications

Education

Undergraduate degree in Finance, Economics, Engineering, Accounting, or a quantitative field required; MBA, CFA, or equivalent advanced credential preferred.

Experience

8-10+ years in capital markets, corporate banking, credit portfolio management, treasury, balance sheet management, transaction structuring, distribution, or risk management.
Experience with capital allocation, ROE optimization, capital velocity, credit portfolio management, regulatory capital, liquidity and funding optimization, booking models, and structuring solutions.
Demonstrated ability to collaborate with stakeholders and lead cross functional initiatives.

Skills

Expert analytical, financial modeling, structuring, optimization, and risk assessment capabilities, with deep knowledge of OSFI and global regulatory capital, liquidity, and funding frameworks.
Exceptional stakeholder management, communication, and influence skills.
Strong strategic and structuring orientation, with the ability to translate complex and interdependent capital, liquidity, tax, risk, and business considerations into executable solutions.

new_jobs.title: Director, Product
new_jobs.description:
Client Summary

O2E Brands is the parent company behind three exceptional brands: 1-800-GOT-JUNK?, WOW 1 DAY PAINTING, and Shack Shine. Their core philosophy is “It’s All About People.” They operate with transparency, trust, and a growth mindset. 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? is widely recognized as the world’s largest junk-removal franchise, helping both homes and businesses reclaim space with efficient, full‑service junk removal. Backed by a visionary CEO, the company has since grown into a powerhouse in its category, operating in major metros across North America and Australia.

1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? isn’t just a junk-hauling company — it’s a scalable, high-growth franchise brand. Their financial performance, operational footprint, and consistent expansion reflect deep market penetration and strong business fundamentals.

Behind the trucks is a growing product and technology organization. O2E runs an agile product operating model in which product managers, engineers and designers work together in trios. The company is now building much of its own software from scratch, including the systems franchise partners use to run their businesses every day: dispatch, routing, capacity, and the apps crews use in the field.

Now entering the next major chapter, they’re on a mission to double the business from approximately $700M to $1.4B by transforming from a single-service brand into a multi-product, customer-obsessed growth platform. With one of North America’s most recognized and beloved brands, an energized franchise network, and a clear path to multi-business expansion, the company is poised for its most ambitious decade yet.

Highlights

Founded in 1989, HQ in Vancouver, BC
Part of the O2E Brands umbrella, founded by CEO Brian Scudamore
Brian has been featured on Oprah for his leadership, Undercover Boss, Forbes, The Wall Street Journal, The Globe and Mail, and most recently as a Dragon on Dragon's Den!
Recognized locally as a “Most Admired Corporate Culture”, a “Top 50 Small & Medium Employer”, and a “Most Engaged Workplace.”
Ranked #8 on the 2026 Top 100 Global Most Loved Workplaces®
Recognized nationally as a workplace of choice through numerous awards, including “Best Place to Work”, “Great Workplaces in Canada”, and “50 Most Engaged Workplaces.”
175 locations across Canada, the United States, and Australia
Brian Scudamore was recognized as a Top Most Loved CEO in 2024
An agile product org built on trios of PM, engineering, and design, now building new products in-house

About the Role

1-800-GOT-JUNK? is building the operational backbone for its next chapter of growth. As the business scales across a large franchise network, the systems and processes that power its operations need to be standardized, connected, and built to scale. This role leads that work, shaping the internal tools that corporate staff and front-line team members rely on every day.
Reporting to the SVP, Product, we are looking for a Director of Product (Back Office) to lead the unified product strategy and execution across Platform, Data, the Operator Portal, and the Truck Team Member (TTM) app. You will own back-office standardization and process transformation, with the goal of building scalable, reliable internal tools that maximize operational efficiency across the system.
You will lead a team of senior product managers and product managers, and ensure key stakeholders, including large franchise ownership groups with established business operations, are aligned and moving in the same direction.

Please note: this role is hybrid and based in either Kansas City (Overland Park, KS) or Vancouver, BC.

Product Strategy & Execution:

Serve as the product leadership voice for the unified back-office strategy, translating the company’s Winning Aspiration, Where We Play, and How We Win strategy into a coherent product roadmap and execution plan
Ensure the team is focused on the highest-leverage problems, without spreading effort across too many priorities
Pressure-test team approaches by challenging assumptions, validating customer insight, and grounding decisions in customer truth and the Product & Technology Strategy
Connect product strategy to operational and go-to-market realities

Process Transformation & Standardization:

Map all as-is and to-be processes across the product function using swim lane and value stream mapping, doing the work yourself
Identify overlap, gaps, and inconsistencies in how teams work, and give the SVP a clear view of what everyone does today and what they should be doing
Build a sequenced transformation roadmap that moves the org from current state to a standardized target state
Drive standardization across residential and commercial product teams in partnership with other product leaders

AI & Product Innovation:

Bring a real point of view on how AI can change product discovery, prototyping and operational workflows, well beyond conversational tools
Introduce AI tools and practices that help standardize and speed up how the product org works
Help shape how AI shows up in the products franchise partners and crews use every day

Team Leadership & Capacity Building:

Lead and develop the back-office product team, including senior product managers and product managers
Build a team environment where PMs operate with clarity, autonomy, and strong strategic context
Identify capability or capacity gaps early and flag them to the SVP, Product

Stakeholder Management & Franchise Alignment:

Ensure key stakeholders, including large franchise ownership groups, are aligned and moving in the same direction
Create a clear and respectful path for integrating franchise expertise into the formal product and revenue model
Communicate progress, decisions, and trade-offs clearly to franchise executive stakeholders, managing expectations through a period of significant change
Represent product priorities in senior leadership conversations and cross-functional planning

Organizational Agility & Decision Quality:

Keep teams moving by surfacing blockers, resolving ambiguity, and escalating where needed
Bring the right people into the right conversations at the right time
Maintain a clear view of what is decided, what is in progress, and what is still open across the product agenda

About You

You're a senior product leader who's built software for field operations and isn't afraid to roll up your sleeves. You've spent your career in tech, working closely with engineers and designers to bring new products to life, and the operational side of a business energizes you. You have the presence to hold a room of franchise owners, the empathy to actually listen to them, and the conviction not to get walked over.

10+ years in product management, including 5+ years leading and developing PMs
Hands-on experience with process transformation, including swim lane and/or value stream mapping you've done yourself, not delegated
Product experience in field operations software such as dispatch, routing, scheduling, fleet, capacity management or similar operational platforms
Background in a SaaS or tech environment, building software in an agile model and embedded with engineering and design (trio, pod or squad)
A track record of building and launching new products, not just configuring existing tools
Real AI fluency and a point of view on how it changes product work, with tools you've used and an opinion on what's good
Executive presence and adaptable communication, with experience earning buy-in from external or franchise stakeholders

Bonus:

Experience with Snowflake or a similar modern data stack
Franchise, multi-location or field services industry exposure
Lean or Six Sigma training
Experience standing up product operations practices across an org

The Extras that Matter

1-800-GOT-JUNK? is famous for its culture, and for good reason. This is a place that takes people seriously and builds things that matter to thousands of franchise partners and crews.
A direct line to the CEO's priorities, and the chance to build the operational backbone of an iconic brand
Competitive compensation package
Company Profit Sharing Program
401(k): employer match up to 4% (US)
Comprehensive Extended Health & Dental Benefits
Generous paid vacation and personal days
Hybrid work environment (Overland Park, KS or Vancouver, BC)
Professional development opportunities
Health & Wellness programs

Compensation:
Base salary of $180K–$200K in local currency

Erik Church - President & COO
Renato Jose Mascardo - CTO
Kathy Miller - SVP, Global Product
Kristy Pennock - SVP, People & Culture

Detailed Job Description

Position Overview

The Executive Director of Finance is responsible for providing strategic leadership and comprehensive oversight of the company’s financial management functions, including financial planning, budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, cash flow management, financial analysis, and internal financial controls. This role ensures that the company’s financial operations are aligned with its overall strategic objectives, while supporting organizational growth, profitability enhancement, and long-term financial stability.

The Executive Director of Finance works closely with the Chief Financial Officer (CFO), Chief Executive Officer (CEO), senior management team, department heads, and business unit managers to develop financial strategies, evaluate business performance, manage financial resources, and provide support for key management decisions. This position plays a critical role in strengthening financial governance, improving the efficiency of financial management, and ensuring the accuracy and transparency of the company’s financial operations.

Key Responsibilities

I. Financial Strategy and Senior Leadership

Develop and implement financial strategies that align with the company’s business objectives, operational priorities, and long-term development plans. Provide financial guidance to senior management regarding investment decisions, resource allocation, cost management, and business expansion opportunities. Establish financial policies, management standards, and performance targets to strengthen financial discipline and ensure that all financial activities remain consistent with the company’s overall strategy.

II. Financial Planning, Budgeting, and Forecasting

Take full responsibility for the preparation and execution of annual budgets, periodic financial forecasts, and long-term financial plans. Coordinate with department heads and business unit leaders to set financial targets, assess capital requirements, and allocate financial resources effectively. Continuously monitor budget execution, analyze financial variances, and propose corrective or improvement measures to maintain cost efficiency and achieve established financial goals.

III. Financial Reporting and Performance Analysis

Oversee the preparation, review, and submission of monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports. Ensure that financial statements, management reports, and performance analysis data are accurate, timely, and compliant with applicable accounting standards. Evaluate the company’s revenue performance, operating expenses, profitability, cash flow, and financial trends to provide actionable insights that support senior management decision-making and the improvement of business performance.

IV. Cash Flow and Financial Resource Management

Supervise cash flow planning, working capital management, liquidity monitoring, and the allocation of financial resources. Establish relevant management procedures to ensure the company maintains sufficient cash reserves, fulfills its financial obligations, and meets the requirements of daily business operations. Collaborate with treasury, accounting, and banking partners to optimize cash management practices, monitor capital requirements, and strengthen the company’s overall financial position.

V. Financial Risk Management and Internal Control

Establish and maintain a robust system of financial controls, risk management procedures, and corporate financial governance standards. Identify and assess potential financial risks related to expenditures, investments, credit, liquidity, and operational activities. Work with internal audit, compliance, legal, and accounting teams to strengthen internal controls, address anomalies in financial management, and ensure that financial processes adhere to company policies and relevant regulatory requirements.

VI. Investment Evaluation and Strategic Financial Support

Conduct financial evaluations of business expansion plans, capital investment proposals, strategic projects, and potential mergers and acquisitions. Develop financial models to analyze return on investment (ROI), assess the financial feasibility of projects, and provide professional recommendations to senior management. Collaborate with the Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and the senior leadership team to support capital allocation decisions, financial restructuring initiatives, and other strategic corporate development activities.

VII. Financial Compliance and Coordination with External Stakeholders

Ensure that the company’s financial management activities comply with applicable accounting standards, tax requirements, regulatory obligations, and corporate governance policies. Coordinate with external auditors, tax advisors, financial institutions, and other professional service providers as necessary. Oversee the preparation of financial documentation, audit materials, and compliance reports to ensure transparency and accountability in financial operations.

VIII. Financial Leadership and Process Improvement

Lead and develop the company’s finance team, encompassing functions such as financial planning, accounting, financial reporting, and financial analysis. Define departmental objectives, performance standards, staff development plans, and operational accountability mechanisms. Evaluate financial management systems, reporting technologies, and business processes to enhance operational efficiency, improve the accuracy of financial data, and drive continuous improvement within the finance function.

Qualifications

Education

A bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, economics, business administration, or a related field is required. A master’s degree in finance, accounting, or business administration (MBA) is preferred. Preference will be given to candidates who hold professional qualifications such as Certified Public Accountant (CPA), Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA), or Certified Management Accountant (CMA).

Work Experience

Typically, candidates should possess 15 to 18 or more years of progressively responsible experience in finance, accounting, financial planning, or corporate financial management, including at least 5 years in a senior financial management or executive leadership role.

Candidates must have extensive experience in overseeing financial planning and analysis (FP&A), budgeting, financial forecasting, financial reporting, cash flow management, internal controls, and financial risk assessment. They should demonstrate the ability to lead finance teams, manage complex financial operations, develop financial strategies, and provide expert decision-making advice to senior management. Preference will be given to those with experience in supporting business expansion, capital investment decisions, organizational restructuring, or financial management across multiple business units.
